passages.t: ‘Lead me to the rock that is higher than I’
passages.happening:
The heading reads, “For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David” (verse 1). The prayer is short and simple. “Hear my cry, O God; attend to my prayer” (verse 1).

The one praying feels far away. “From the ends of the earth I call out to You whenever my heart is faint. Lead me to the rock that is higher than I” (verse 2). He remembers that God has been his refuge before (verse 3). He asks for one thing: “Let me dwell in Your tent forever and take refuge in the shelter of Your wings” (verse 4).

Then the prayer turns to the king. “Increase the days of the king’s life; may his years span many generations” (verse 6). “May he sit enthroned in God’s presence forever” (verse 7). It ends with a promise to praise God “day by day” (verse 8).
passages.hearers:
‘The ends of the earth’ may mean real distance, or it may mean feeling cut off. No occasion is given. One old suggestion is David's time across the Jordan, when he fled from Absalom. Others think of a soldier or an exile praying for himself and his king.

‘A rock higher than I’ is a picture from the hill country. In danger you climbed to high rock where attackers could not reach. The psalmist cannot climb it alone. He asks to be led there.

In the ancient world a guest in someone's tent came under the host's protection. To ‘dwell in Your tent’ was to be God's guest, safe under his name. ‘The shelter of Your wings’ is the picture of a bird covering its young, which Psalm 57 also uses.

The prayer for the king's life to ‘span many generations’ asks more than any one king could have. That is one reason it was later read as a prayer for David's whole line, and, by Christians, of the king who reigns forever. The book page explains the royal psalms.
passages.later:
Isaiah pictures a good ruler as “the shadow of a great rock in an arid land” (Isaiah 32:2).

The New Testament asks Christians to pray “for kings and all those in authority” (1 Timothy 2:2). Like Psalm 61, it is a prayer for those who rule, not worship of them.
passages.asks:
‘Higher than I’ is the heart of this psalm. When your heart is faint, you cannot lift yourself. You need something firmer than you are, and someone to lead you to it.

This is a good prayer for days when you feel far from God. You can pray verse 2 from wherever ‘the ends of the earth’ are for you. And verse 8 shows the answer: faithfulness ‘day by day’, not all at once.
